sentences.zh: 高宗諸子

translations.literal: The sons of Emperor Gaozong
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Emperor Gaozong

sentences.zh: 高宗八男：則天順聖皇后生中宗、睿宗及孝敬皇帝弘、章懷太子賢，後宮劉氏生燕王忠，鄭氏生原王孝，楊氏生澤王上金，蕭淑妃生許王素節。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong had eight sons: Empress Zetian the Shunsheng gave birth to Zhongzong, Ruizong, Emperor Xiaojing Hong, and Crown Prince Zhanghuai Xian; the rear-palace Lady Liu gave birth to Prince of Yan Zhong; Lady Zheng gave birth to Prince Yuan Xiao; Lady Yang gave birth to Prince of Ze Shangjin; Consort Xiao Shufei gave birth to Prince of Xu Sujie.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong had eight sons. Empress Wu Zetian bore Zhongzong, Ruizong, Emperor Xiaojing Hong, and Crown Prince Zhanghuai Xian. Lady Liu of the inner palace bore Prince of Yan Zhong; Lady Zheng bore Prince Yuan Xiao; Lady Yang bore Prince of Ze Shangjin; and Consort Xiao Shufei bore Prince of Xu Sujie.

sentences.zh: 燕王 忠

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Zhong
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yan Zhong

sentences.zh: 燕王忠，字正本，高宗長子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Zhong, style name Zhengben, was Emperor Gaozong's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yan Zhong, whose style name was Zhengben, was the eldest son of Emperor Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 高宗初入東宮而生忠，宴宮僚於弘教殿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong first entered the Eastern Palace, Zhong was born, and he feasted the palace staff in Hongjiao Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was born soon after Gaozong entered the Eastern Palace as heir apparent, and the emperor held a feast for palace officials in Hongjiao Hall.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸宮，顧謂宮臣曰：“頃來王業稍可，非無酒食，而唐突卿等宴會者，朕初有此孫，故相就為樂耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong visited the palace and, turning to the palace officials, said: "Recently the royal enterprise has improved somewhat; it is not that wine and food are lacking, yet I have presumptuously troubled you with this feast because I have this grandson for the first time and wished to share the joy with you."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong visited the palace, he said to the palace officials: "The realm has lately been in fair order, and it is not as though wine and food are scarce; yet I have taken the liberty of summoning you to this feast because I have my first grandson and wished to celebrate with you."

sentences.zh: ”太宗酒酣起舞，以屬群臣，在位於是遍舞，盡日而罷，賜物有差。

translations.literal: " When Taizong, flushed with wine, rose to dance and handed the dance to the assembled ministers, all those present thereupon danced in turn; the revel lasted the whole day before ending, and gifts were bestowed in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong, well into his cups, rose to dance and passed the lead to his ministers, everyone present danced in turn. The celebration lasted all day, and gifts were distributed according to rank.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十年，封為陳王。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In 646 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，拜雍州牧。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui, he was appointed Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 650 he was appointed Governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時王皇后無子，其舅中書令柳奭說後謀立忠為皇太子，以忠母賤，冀其親己，後然之。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Wang had no son; her uncle, Chief Minister of the Secretariat Liu Shi, urged the empress to plot making Zhong crown prince, reasoning that because Zhong's mother was of low status he would be drawn close to her; the empress agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang was childless, and her uncle Liu Shi, Chief Minister of the Secretariat, urged her to have Zhong named crown prince, arguing that because his mother was of humble birth he would remain close to the empress. She agreed.

sentences.zh: 奭與尚書右僕射褚遂良、侍中韓瑗諷、太尉長孫無忌、右僕射於誌寧等，固請立忠為儲後，高宗許之。

translations.literal: Liu Shi, together with Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Chu Suiliang, Palace Attendant Han Yuan, Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Right Vice Director Yu Zhining, and others, earnestly petitioned to establish Zhong as heir apparent, and Emperor Gaozong consented.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi joined Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Zhangsun Wuji, Yu Zhining, and others in pressing Gaozong to name Zhong heir apparent, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 三年，立忠為皇太子，大赦天下，五品已上子為父後者賜勳一級。

translations.literal: In the third year, Zhong was established as crown prince; a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm, and sons of fifth rank and above who were heirs to their fathers were granted one grade of merit.
translations.idiomatic: In 652 Zhong was named crown prince. A general amnesty was declared, and heirs of officials of fifth rank and above received one grade of merit.

sentences.zh: 六年，加元服，製大辟罪已下並降一等，大酺三日。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he received the cap of manhood; an edict reduced all crimes below capital punishment by one degree, and great feasting was held for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In 655 he came of age. Capital crimes and all lesser offenses were reduced by one degree, and the court held three days of public celebration.

sentences.zh: 其年，王皇后被廢，武昭儀所生皇子弘年三歲。

translations.literal: That same year Empress Wang was deposed, and the prince Hong born to Lady Wu Zhaoyi was three years old.
translations.idiomatic: That year Empress Wang was deposed, and Lady Wu's son Hong was three years old.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書許敬宗希旨上疏曰：“伏惟陛下憲章千古，含育萬邦，爰立聖慈，母儀天下。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong, seeking to please, submitted a memorial saying: "I humbly consider that Your Majesty's statutes illumine the ages and nurture the myriad realms; you have established a sage and loving consort who embodies motherhood for the world."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong, Minister of Rites, submitted a flattering memorial: "Your Majesty's laws illumine the ages and nurture all lands; you have raised a sage and loving consort who embodies motherhood for the realm."

sentences.zh: 既而皇后生子，合處少陽。

translations.literal: Now that the empress has borne a son, he ought to occupy the position of lesser yang.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the empress has borne a son, he rightly belongs in the eastern palace of the heir.

sentences.zh: 出自塗山，是謂吾君之胤；

translations.literal: Born from Tushan, he is truly the heir of our lord;
translations.idiomatic: Born of Tushan, he is truly our sovereign's heir;

sentences.zh: 夙聞胎教，宜展問豎之心。

translations.literal: long versed in prenatal instruction, he should display the heart of one who inquires after his tutor.
translations.idiomatic: reared from the womb in virtue, he should show the mind eager to learn from his teachers.

sentences.zh: 乃復為孽奪宗，降居藩邸，是使前星匿彩，瑤嶽韜峰。

translations.literal: yet again a bastard has seized the succession and been demoted to a princely residence, causing the former star to hide its brilliance and the jade peak to veil its splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a lesser son again holds the succession while the true heir is sent to a princely residence, dimming the heir's star and hiding the jade mountain's peak.

sentences.zh: 臣以愚誠，竊所未喻。

translations.literal: Your servant, in his foolish sincerity, privately fails to understand this.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble sincerity I cannot understand this.

sentences.zh: 且今之守器，素非皇嫡，永徽爰始，國本未生，權引彗星，越升明兩。

translations.literal: Moreover, the present holder of the vessel was never the legitimate imperial son; from the beginning of Yonghui, when the foundation of the state had not yet been born, a comet was provisionally drawn forth to ascend beyond the bright pair.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the present heir was never the legitimate son. From the start of Yonghui, before the true heir was born, a comet was provisionally elevated above the rightful pair.

sentences.zh: 近者元妃載誕，正胤降神，重光日融，爝暉宜息。

translations.literal: Recently the primary consort has given birth; the legitimate heir has descended as a spirit; the doubled radiance of the sun should merge, and the torchlight ought to be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the chief consort has borne a son; the true heir has come down from heaven. The sun's doubled light should shine as one, and the lesser flame ought to be put out.

sentences.zh: 安可以茲傍統，叨據溫文？

translations.literal: How can this collateral succession presumptuously occupy the gentle and cultured role?
translations.idiomatic: How can this collateral line presumptuously hold the heir's place?

sentences.zh: 國有諍臣，孰逃其責！

translations.literal: When the state has remonstrating ministers, who can escape this duty!
translations.idiomatic: When the state has ministers who speak plainly, who can shirk this duty!

sentences.zh: 竊惟息姑克讓，可以思齊；

translations.literal: I privately reflect that Xigong's capacity for yielding offers a model for emulation;
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that Xigong's willingness to yield offers a model to follow;

sentences.zh: 劉強守藩，宜遵往軌。

translations.literal: Liu Qiang's guarding of his fief ought to follow the former track.
translations.idiomatic: and Liu Qiang's holding to his fief should follow precedent.

sentences.zh: 追跡太伯，不亦休哉？

translations.literal: To follow in the footsteps of Taibo—would that not be excellent?
translations.idiomatic: To follow Taibo's example—would that not be excellent?

sentences.zh: 踵武延陵，故常安矣。

translations.literal: Treading in the martial wake of Yanling, one would ever be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Following Yanling's path, all would remain secure.

sentences.zh: 寧可反植枝幹，久易位於天庭；

translations.literal: How can one plant branches upside down and long exchange positions in the celestial court;
translations.idiomatic: How can branches be planted upside down and positions in the court long be reversed;

sentences.zh: 倒襲衣裳，使違方於震位？

translations.literal: invert upper and lower garments and set what is improper in the position of Zhen?
translations.idiomatic: or garments be worn inside out so that the improper occupies the heir's place?

sentences.zh: 蠢爾黎庶，雲誰係心？

translations.literal: Your dull common people—upon whom do their hearts depend?
translations.idiomatic: The common people—upon whom will their hearts depend?

sentences.zh: 垂裕後昆，將何播美？

translations.literal: In bestowing abundance on later generations, what beauty will you spread abroad?
translations.idiomatic: What glory will you leave to posterity?

sentences.zh: ”高宗從之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozong followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，廢忠為梁王，授梁州都督，賜實封二千戶，物二萬段，甲第一區。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing, Zhong was deposed and made Prince of Liang, appointed Military Commissioner of Liangzhou, granted a substantive fief of two thousand households, twenty thousand bolts of goods, and one first-rank suit of armor.
translations.idiomatic: In 656 Zhong was deposed and made Prince of Liang, with appointment as commissioner of Liangzhou, a substantive fief of two thousand households, twenty thousand bolts of goods, and a suit of first-rank armor.

sentences.zh: 其年，轉房州刺史。

translations.literal: That same year he was transferred to be Prefect of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was transferred to Prefect of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 原王 孝

translations.literal: Prince Yuan Xiao
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Xiao

sentences.zh: 原王孝，高宗第二子也。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan Xiao was Emperor Gaozong's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Xiao was Gaozong's second son.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，封許王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In 650 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜并州都督。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Military Commissioner of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 652 he was appointed commissioner of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年，累除遂州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing he was successively removed and made Prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 658 he was appointed Prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 麟德元年薨，贈益州大都督，諡曰悼。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longde he died; posthumously he was given Grand Military Commissioner of Yizhou, with the posthumous name Dao.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 664 and was posthumously made Grand Commissioner of Yizhou, with the posthumous name Dao (Lamented).

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追贈原王、司徒、益州大都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Yuan, Minister of Education, and Grand Military Commissioner of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Yuan, Minister of Education, and Grand Commissioner of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 澤王 上金

translations.literal: Prince of Ze Shangjin
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ze Shangjin

sentences.zh: 澤王上金，高宗第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Ze Shangjin was Emperor Gaozong's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ze Shangjin was Gaozong's third son.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，封杞王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui he was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In 650 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 三年，遙授益州大都督。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed in absentia as Grand Military Commissioner of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 652 he was appointed in absentia as Grand Commissioner of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 乾封元年，累轉壽州刺史，有罪免官，削封邑，仍於澧州安置。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng he was successively transferred to Prefect of Shouzhou; for an offense he was dismissed from office, his fief was reduced, and he was nevertheless settled at Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 666 he was made Prefect of Shouzhou. After an offense he was dismissed, his fief was reduced, and he was confined at Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 上金既為則天所惡，所司希旨，求索罪失以奏之，故有此黜。

translations.literal: Because Shangjin was already detested by Zetian, the responsible offices, seeking to please her, searched out faults and offenses to report, and therefore this dismissal occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian already disliked Shangjin, and the responsible offices, eager to please her, hunted for faults to report—hence this dismissal.

sentences.zh: 永隆二年二月，則天矯抗表杞王上金、鄱陽王素節許同朝集之例，義陽、宣城二公主緣母蕭氏獲譴，從夫外官，請授官職。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Yonglong, Zetian forged a memorial of protest allowing Prince of Qi Shangjin and Prince of Poyang Sujie the precedent of attending court assemblies; the two princesses of Yiyang and Xuancheng, because their mother Lady Xiao had been punished, followed their husbands in external offices and requested appointment to posts.
translations.idiomatic: In February 681 Wu Zetian forged a memorial allowing Princes Qi Shangjin and Poyang Sujie to attend court assemblies. The princesses of Yiyang and Xuancheng, whose mother Consort Xiao had been punished, had followed their husbands into provincial service and now requested official posts.

sentences.zh: 以上金為沔州刺史，素節為岳州刺史，仍不預朝集。

translations.literal: Shangjin was made Prefect of Mianzhou and Sujie Prefect of Yuezhou, yet they still did not participate in court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjin was made Prefect of Mianzhou and Sujie Prefect of Yuezhou, but they were still barred from court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖元年，上金、素節，義陽、宣城二公主聽赴哀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Sisheng, Shangjin, Sujie, and the two princesses of Yiyang and Xuancheng were permitted to come for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In 684 Shangjin, Sujie, and the princesses of Yiyang and Xuancheng were permitted to attend the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 文明元年，上金封畢王，素節封為葛王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wenming, Shangjin was enfeoffed as Prince of Bi and Sujie as Prince of Ge.
translations.idiomatic: In 684 Shangjin was enfeoffed as Prince of Bi and Sujie as Prince of Ge.

sentences.zh: 又改上金封為澤王、蘇州刺史，素節許王、隆州刺史。

translations.literal: Shangjin's fief was again changed to Prince of Ze and Prefect of Suzhou; Sujie was made Prince of Xu and Prefect of Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjin was then made Prince of Ze and Prefect of Suzhou; Sujie was made Prince of Xu and Prefect of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 垂拱元年，改陳州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chuigong he was changed to Prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 685 he was transferred to Prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，授太子左衛率，出為隨州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang he was appointed Left Leader of the Crown Prince's Guard and sent out as Prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 689 he was appointed Left Leader of the Crown Prince's Guard and sent out as Prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 載初元年，武承嗣使酷吏周興誣告上金、素節謀反，召至都，係於御史台。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zaichu, Wu Chengsi had the cruel official Zhou Xing falsely accuse Shangjin and Sujie of plotting rebellion; they were summoned to the capital and detained at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In 689 Wu Chengsi had the notorious investigator Zhou Xing accuse Shangjin and Sujie of treason. They were summoned to the capital and imprisoned at the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 舒州刺史、許王素節見殺於都城南驛，因害其支黨。

translations.literal: Sujie, Prince of Xu and Prefect of Shuzhou, was killed at the southern relay station of the capital, and his collateral kin were harmed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xu Sujie, Prefect of Shuzhou, was killed at the southern relay station outside the capital, and his kin were destroyed as well.

sentences.zh: 上金恐懼，自縊死。

translations.literal: Shangjin, in fear, hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Shangjin hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 子義珍、義玫、義璋、義環、義瑾、義遂七人並配流顯州而死。

translations.literal: His seven sons Yizhen, Yimei, Yizhang, Yihuan, Yijin, and Yisui were all banished to Xianzhou and died there.
translations.idiomatic: His seven sons Yizhen, Yimei, Yizhang, Yihuan, Yijin, and Yisui were all exiled to Xianzhou and died there.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追復上金官爵，封庶子義珣為嗣澤王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, Shangjin's offices and titles were posthumously restored, and his son by a concubine Yixun was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era Shangjin's titles were posthumously restored, and his son by a concubine, Yixun, was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Ze.

sentences.zh: 先是，義珣竄在嶺外，匿於傭保之間。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yixun had fled beyond the Ling range and hid among hired laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yixun had fled south of the mountains and hidden among hired laborers.

sentences.zh: 及紹封無幾，有人告義珣非上金子，假冒襲爵。

translations.literal: Not long after he was enfeoffed as heir, someone reported that Yixun was not Shangjin's son and had falsely assumed the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after his enfeoffment someone reported that Yixun was not Shangjin's son and had fraudulently claimed the title.

sentences.zh: 義珣不能自明，復流於嶺外。

translations.literal: Yixun could not clear himself and was again exiled beyond the Ling range.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to clear himself, Yixun was exiled south again.

sentences.zh: 開元初，封素節子璆為嗣澤王，繼上金後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Sujie's son Qiu was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Ze to succeed Shangjin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era Sujie's son Qiu was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Ze to succeed Shangjin.

sentences.zh: 十二年，玉真公主表稱義珣實上金遺胤，被嗣許王瓘兄弟利其封爵，謀構廢之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Princess Yuzhen submitted a memorial stating that Yixun was truly Shangjin's surviving heir and had been plotted against and deposed by the brothers of Heir Prince of Xu Guan, who coveted his fief and title.
translations.idiomatic: In 724 Princess Yuzhen memorialized that Yixun was truly Shangjin's surviving heir and had been framed by Heir Prince of Xu Guan and his brothers, who coveted his title.

sentences.zh: 今上由是削璆王爵，復召義珣為嗣澤王，拜率更令。

translations.literal: The present emperor thereupon stripped Qiu of his princely rank, recalled Yixun as Heir Prince of Ze, and appointed him Director of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon stripped Qiu of his title, recalled Yixun as Heir Prince of Ze, and appointed him Director of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 因是，諸宗室非本宗襲爵，自中興已後繼為嗣王者，皆令歸宗，削其爵邑也。

translations.literal: Because of this, all members of the imperial clan who had succeeded to titles outside their own lineage and, since the restoration, had continued as heir princes were ordered to return to their original houses, and their titles and fiefs were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all imperial clansmen who had inherited titles outside their own line since the restoration were ordered back to their original houses and stripped of their fiefs.

sentences.zh: 許王 素節

translations.literal: Prince of Xu Sujie
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xu Sujie

sentences.zh: 許王素節，高宗第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Xu Sujie was Emperor Gaozong's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xu Sujie was Gaozong's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 年六歲，永徽二年，封雍王，尋授雍州牧。

translations.literal: At age six, in the second year of Yonghui, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong and soon appointed Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At age six, in 651, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong and soon appointed Governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 素節能日誦古詩賦五百餘言，受業於學十徐齊聃，精勤不倦，高宗甚愛之。

translations.literal: Sujie could recite more than five hundred words of ancient poetry and rhapsodies each day; he studied under Academician Xu Qidan, diligent and untiring, and Emperor Gaozong loved him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Sujie could recite more than five hundred lines of classical poetry a day. He studied under Academician Xu Qidan with tireless diligence, and Gaozong doted on him.

sentences.zh: 又轉岐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 年十二，改封郇王。

translations.literal: At age twelve he was changed to Prince of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xun.

sentences.zh: 初，則天未為皇后也，與素節母蕭淑妃爭寵，遞相譖毀。

translations.literal: Earlier, before Zetian became empress, she and Sujie's mother Consort Xiao Shufei competed for favor and slandered each other in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wu Zetian became empress, she and Sujie's mother Consort Xiao Shufei had vied for the emperor's favor and slandered each other.

sentences.zh: 六年，則天立為皇后後，淑妃竟為則天所譖毀，幽辱而殺之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, after Zetian was established as empress, Shufei was ultimately slandered by Zetian, confined and humiliated, and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In 655, after Wu became empress, Shufei was ultimately framed, imprisoned, and killed.

sentences.zh: 素節尤被讒嫉，出為申州刺史。

translations.literal: Sujie was especially subject to slander and jealousy and was sent out as Prefect of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sujie was especially targeted by slander and was sent out as Prefect of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾封初，下敕曰：“素節既舊疾患，宜不須入朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfeng an edict was issued: "Since Sujie has long-standing illness, he need not come to court."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianfeng era an edict declared: "Because Sujie has long been ill, he need not attend court."

sentences.zh: ”而素節實無疾。

translations.literal: " Yet Sujie was in fact free of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In fact he was not ill at all.

sentences.zh: 素節自以久乖朝覲，遂著《忠孝論》以見意，詞多不載。

translations.literal: Sujie, considering that he had long been absent from court audiences, thereupon composed the "Treatise on Loyalty and Filial Piety" to express his intent; most of its wording is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Believing he had long been barred from court, Sujie wrote the Treatise on Loyalty and Filial Piety to express his grievance; most of its text is not preserved here.

sentences.zh: 時王府倉曹參軍張柬之因使潛封此論以進，則天見之，逾不悅，誣以贓賄，降封鄱陽郡王，仍於袁州安置。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Jianzhi, Registrar of the Princely Household's Granary, used an envoy to secretly seal and submit this treatise; when Zetian saw it she was all the more displeased, falsely charged him with bribery, reduced his rank to Prince of Poyang Commandery, and nevertheless settled him at Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianzhi, a staff officer of the princely household, had the treatise secretly submitted. Wu Zetian was further enraged, falsely charged him with bribery, reduced him to Prince of Poyang, and confined him at Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年，禁錮終身，又改於岳州安置。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yifeng he was imprisoned for life and again transferred to confinement at Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 677 he was imprisoned for life and transferred to confinement at Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 永隆元年，轉岳州刺史，後改封葛王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonglong he was transferred to Prefect of Yuezhou and later changed to Prince of Ge.
translations.idiomatic: In 680 he was made Prefect of Yuezhou and later re-enfeoffed as Prince of Ge.

sentences.zh: 則天稱製，又進封許王，累除舒州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zetian assumed the imperial title, he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Xu and successively removed to Prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zetian took the throne he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Xu and appointed Prefect of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 天授中，與上金同被誣告，追赴都。

translations.literal: During the Tian shou era he was, like Shangjin, falsely accused and summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tian shou era he was, like Shangjin, falsely accused of treason and summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 臨發州，聞有遭喪哭者，謂左右曰：“病死何由可得，更何須哭！

translations.literal: As he was about to leave the prefecture, hearing someone wailing for a bereavement, he said to those beside him: "Death by illness—how could one obtain that? Why need one weep further!"
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving his post he heard funeral wailing and said to his attendants: "How could I hope to die of illness? Why bother weeping!"

sentences.zh: ”行至都城南龍門驛，被縊死，年四十三，則天令以庶人禮葬之。

translations.literal: " When he reached Longmen Relay south of the capital he was strangled; he was forty-three years old, and Zetian ordered him buried with commoner rites.
translations.idiomatic: At Longmen Relay south of the capital he was strangled. He was forty-three. Wu Zetian ordered him buried with commoner rites.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，追封許王，贈開府儀同三司、許州刺史，仍以禮改葬，陪於乾陵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xu, given the gift of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with First-Class Honors, and made Prefect of Xuzhou; he was reburied with proper rites and interred beside Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne, Sujie was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xu, given the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with First-Class Honors, and reburied with full rites beside Qianling.

sentences.zh: 素節被殺之時，子瑛、琬、璣、瑒等九人並為則天所殺，惟少子琳、瓘、璆、欽古以年小，特令長禁雷州。

translations.literal: When Sujie was killed, his nine sons Ying, Wan, Ji, Yang, and others were all killed by Zetian; only the younger sons Lin, Guan, Qiu, and Qingu, because they were young, were specially ordered to lifelong confinement at Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Sujie was killed, nine of his sons including Ying, Wan, Ji, and Yang were executed. Only the younger sons Lin, Guan, Qiu, and Qingu, being still young, were sentenced to lifelong confinement at Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，封瓘為嗣許王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, Guan was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era Guan was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 開元初，封琳為嗣越王，以紹越王貞之後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Lin was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Yue to continue the line of Prince of Yue Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era Lin was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Yue to continue the line of Prince Zhen.

sentences.zh: 璆為嗣澤王，以繼伯父澤王上金之後。

translations.literal: Qiu was made Heir Prince of Ze to succeed his paternal uncle Prince of Ze Shangjin.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was made Heir Prince of Ze to succeed his uncle Shangjin.

sentences.zh: 琳，官至右監門將軍，卒。

translations.literal: Lin rose to Right Supervisor of the Gate Guards and died.
translations.idiomatic: Lin rose to Right Supervisor of the Gate Guards and died in office.

sentences.zh: 瓘，開元十一年為衛慰卿。

translations.literal: Guan, in the eleventh year of Kaiyuan, became Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In 723 Guan became Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 以抑伯上金男不得承襲，以弟璆繼之，遽譴瓘為鄂州別駕。

translations.literal: To suppress his elder uncle Shangjin's son from inheriting, his younger brother Qiu was made heir, and Guan was hastily demoted to Vice-Prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: To block Shangjin's son from inheriting, his brother Qiu was made heir instead, and Guan was abruptly demoted to Vice-Prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 於是下詔絕其外繼，乃以故澤王上金男義珣為嗣澤王，江王禕為信安郡王，嗣蜀王褕為廣漢郡王，嗣密王徹為濮陽郡王，嗣曹王臻為濟國公，嗣趙王琚為中山郡王，武陽郡王繼宗為澧國公。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ended external succession lines; the former Prince of Ze Shangjin's son Yixun was made Heir Prince of Ze; Prince of Jiang Yi was made Prince of Xin'an Commandery; Heir Prince of Shu Yu was made Prince of Guanghan Commandery; Heir Prince of Mi Che was made Prince of Puyang Commandery; Heir Prince of Cao Zhen was made Duke of Jiguo; Heir Prince of Zhao Ju was made Prince of Zhongshan Commandery; and Prince of Wuyang Commandery Jizong was made Duke of Liguo.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ended external succession lines. Shangjin's son Yixun was made Heir Prince of Ze, and several other princes were given new commandery titles to restore proper succession.

sentences.zh: 瓘累遷邠州刺史、秘書監、守太子詹事。

translations.literal: Guan was successively transferred to Prefect of Binzhou, Director of the Secretariat, and Acting Crown Prince's Household Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was later made Prefect of Binzhou, Director of the Secretariat, and Acting Crown Prince's Household Administrator.

sentences.zh: 璆性仁厚謹願，居家邕睦，朝廷重之。

translations.literal: Qiu's nature was benevolent, generous, and cautious; at home he was harmonious, and the court esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was benevolent, cautious, and harmonious at home, and the court held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 天寶六載卒，贈蜀郡大都督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao he died and was posthumously given Grand Military Commissioner of Shujun.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 747 and was posthumously made Grand Commissioner of Shujun.

sentences.zh: 瓘晚有子，命璆子益為嗣。

translations.literal: Guan had a son late in life and ordered Qiu's son Yi to be his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Guan had a son late in life and named Qiu's son Yi as his heir.

sentences.zh: 及卒，有解、需二子，皆幼孺。

translations.literal: When he died he had two sons, Jie and Xu, both still infants.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he left two infant sons, Jie and Xu.

sentences.zh: 十一載，益襲封許王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Yi inherited the title Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In 752 Yi inherited the title Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 十四載，解娶楊銛女，乃襲許王。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Jie married the daughter of Yang Qian and thereupon inherited as Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In 755 Jie married Yang Qian's daughter and inherited the title Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 璆初為嗣澤王，降為郢國公、宗王卿同正員，特封褒信郡王。

translations.literal: Qiu was first Heir Prince of Ze, then reduced to Duke of Yingguo and Associate Director of the Imperial Clan with full rank, and specially enfeoffed as Prince of Baoxin Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was first Heir Prince of Ze, then reduced to Duke of Ying and Associate Director of the Imperial Clan, and specially enfeoffed as Prince of Baoxin.

sentences.zh: 進《龍池皇德頌》，遷宗正卿、光祿卿、殿中監。

translations.literal: He presented the "Ode to Imperial Virtue at the Dragon Pool" and was transferred to Director of the Imperial Clan, Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Supervisor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He presented the Ode to Imperial Virtue at the Dragon Pool and was promoted to Director of the Imperial Clan, Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Supervisor of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，重拜宗五卿，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was again appointed Director of the Imperial Clan and given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era he was again appointed Director of the Imperial Clan and given the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 璆友弟聰敏，聞善若驚，宗子中有一善，無不薦拔，故宗枝居省闥者，多是璆之所舉。

translations.literal: Qiu was friendly and clever, startled at the mention of good; whenever any clansman had a single merit he recommended and promoted him without fail, so most of the clan branches holding posts in the inner offices were men Qiu had advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was affable and quick-witted, eager to hear of any good deed. He recommended every worthy clansman, and most imperial relatives in high office owed their posts to him.

sentences.zh: 九載卒，贈江陵大都督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died and was posthumously given Grand Military Commissioner of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 750 and was posthumously made Grand Commissioner of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 孝敬皇帝 弘

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaojing Hong
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaojing Hong

sentences.zh: 孝敬皇帝弘，高宗第五子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaojing Hong was Emperor Gaozong's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaojing Hong was Gaozong's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 永徽四年，封代王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yonghui he was enfeoffed as Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In 653 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，立為皇太子，大赦改元。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing he was established as crown prince; a general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title changed.
translations.idiomatic: In 656 he was named crown prince. A general amnesty was declared and the reign title changed.

sentences.zh: 弘嚐受《春秋左氏傳》於率更令郭瑜，至楚子商臣之事，廢卷而歎曰：“此事臣子所不忍聞，經籍聖人垂訓，何故書此？

translations.literal: Hong once received instruction in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals from Director of Astronomy Guo Yu; when he came to the affair of the Chu heir Shangchen, he set aside the scroll and sighed: "This is something subjects cannot bear to hear. The classics are the sage's instruction—why record this?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong studied the Zuo Commentary under Guo Yu, Director of Astronomy. When he reached the story of the Chu heir Shangchen, he set the scroll aside and said: "No loyal subject could bear to hear this. The classics are the sage's teaching—why record such a deed?"

sentences.zh: ”瑜對曰：“孔子修《春秋》，義薦褒貶，故善惡必書。

translations.literal: " Yu replied: "Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals with its principles of praise and blame, so good and evil must both be written."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yu replied: "Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals to praise and blame by principle, so good and evil must both be recorded."

sentences.zh: 褒善以示代，貶惡以誡後，故使商臣之惡，顯於千載。

translations.literal: Praise of the good shows it to later ages; blame of evil warns those who come after, so Shangchen's wickedness is displayed for a thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Good deeds are praised to instruct posterity; evil is condemned to warn those who follow—so Shangchen's crime is known through the ages.

sentences.zh: ”太子曰：“非唯口不可道，故亦耳不忍聞，請改讀餘書。

translations.literal: " The crown prince said: "It is not only that the mouth cannot speak of it—the ears also cannot bear to hear it. Please let me read another book."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said: "I cannot speak of it, nor bear to hear it. Please let me study another text."

sentences.zh: ”瑜再拜賀曰：“裏名勝母，曾子不入；

translations.literal: " Yu bowed twice in congratulation and said: "In a village called Shengmu, Zengzi would not enter;"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yu bowed twice and said: "In a village called Shengmu, Zengzi would not enter;"

sentences.zh: 邑號朝歌，墨子回車。

translations.literal: in a district called Chaoge, Mozi turned his carriage back.
translations.idiomatic: in a place called Chaoge, Mozi turned his carriage back.

sentences.zh: 殿下誠孝冥資，睿情天發，凶悖之跡，黜於視聽。

translations.literal: Your Highness's sincere filial piety is an inborn endowment; your sagely feeling heaven-sent—the traces of wicked rebellion are banished from sight and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's filial piety is inborn and your wisdom heaven-sent; you have banished wicked deeds from your sight and hearing.

sentences.zh: 循奉德音，實深慶躍。

translations.literal: In following your virtuous command I am deeply moved to rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: I am deeply gratified to follow your virtuous command.

sentences.zh: 臣聞安上理人，莫善於禮，非禮無以事天地之神，非禮無以辨君臣之位，故先王重焉。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in securing superiors and governing people nothing is better than ritual; without ritual one cannot serve the spirits of Heaven and Earth, without ritual one cannot distinguish the positions of ruler and subject—therefore the former kings valued it.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that nothing governs people better than ritual. Without ritual one cannot serve Heaven and Earth or define the roles of ruler and subject—hence the former kings prized it.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：‘不學《禮》，無以立。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Without studying the Rites, one cannot establish oneself.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: 'Without studying the Rites, one cannot stand.'

sentences.zh: ’請停《春秋》而讀《禮記》。

translations.literal: ' I beg to set aside the Spring and Autumn and read the Record of Rites instead.
translations.idiomatic: Please set aside the Spring and Autumn and read the Record of Rites instead.

sentences.zh: ”太子從之。

translations.literal: " The crown prince followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince agreed.

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年，命中書令、太子賓客許敬宗，侍中兼太子右庶子許圉師，中書侍郎上官儀，太子中舍人楊思儉等於文思殿博采古今文集，摘其英詞麗句，以類相從，勒成五百卷，名曰《瑤山玉彩》，表上之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longshuo he ordered Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Crown Prince's Guest Xu Jingzong, Palace Attendant and concurrent Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Xu Yanshi, Vice Director of the Secretariat Shangguan Yi, Crown Prince's Attendant Yang Sijian, and others in Wensi Hall broadly to gather ancient and modern literary collections, select their finest phrases and beautiful lines, arrange them by category, compile five hundred scrolls entitled Jade Splendor of Mount Yao, and submit a memorial presenting it.
translations.idiomatic: In 661 he ordered Xu Jingzong, Xu Yanshi, Shangguan Yi, Yang Sijian, and others to compile five hundred scrolls of fine passages from ancient and modern literature, arranged by category, entitled Jade Splendor of Mount Yao, and present it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 製賜物三萬段，敬宗已下加級、賜帛有差。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed thirty thousand bolts of goods; Jingzong and those below him received promotions and silk gifts in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed thirty thousand bolts of goods; Jingzong and the others received promotions and silk gifts according to rank.

sentences.zh: 總章元年二月，親釋菜司成館，因請贈顏回太子少師，曾參太子少保，高宗並從之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Zongzhang he personally performed the vegetable offering at the Directorate of Education and thereupon requested posthumous enfeoffment of Yan Hui as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and Zeng Shen as Junior Guardian to the Crown Prince; Emperor Gaozong approved both.
translations.idiomatic: In February 668 he personally performed the vegetable offering at the Directorate of Education and requested that Yan Hui be posthumously made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and Zeng Shen Junior Guardian; Gaozong approved both.

sentences.zh: 時有敕，征邊遼軍人逃亡限內不首及更有逃亡者，身並處斬，家口沒官。

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered that soldiers in the Liaodong campaign who failed to surrender within the time limit for deserters, and any who deserted thereafter, should all be executed and their households confiscated by the state.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then decreed that soldiers in the Liaodong campaign who failed to surrender within the allotted time, and any further deserters, would be executed and their families confiscated.

sentences.zh: 太子上表諫曰：“竊聞所司以背軍之人，身久不出，家口皆擬沒官。

translations.literal: The crown prince submitted a memorial remonstrating: "I have heard that the responsible offices, regarding men who deserted the army and have long failed to appear, plan to confiscate all their households."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince memorialized: "I hear that offices plan to confiscate the families of soldiers who deserted and have long failed to report."

sentences.zh: 亦有限外出首，未經斷罪，諸州囚禁，人數至多。

translations.literal: There are also those who surrendered within the time limit but have not yet been sentenced; in the various prefectures they are imprisoned, and their number is very great.
translations.idiomatic: Many who surrendered within the time limit remain unsentenced and imprisoned across the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 或臨時遇病，不及軍伍，緣茲怖懼，遂即逃亡；

translations.literal: Some fell suddenly ill and could not reach their units; in terror they thereupon fled;
translations.idiomatic: Some fell ill and could not reach their units, and fled in fear;

sentences.zh: 或因樵采，被賊抄掠；

translations.literal: some while gathering firewood were robbed by bandits;
translations.idiomatic: some were robbed while gathering firewood;

sentences.zh: 或渡海來去，漂沒滄波；

translations.literal: some crossing the sea to and fro were lost in the blue waves;
translations.idiomatic: some crossing the sea were lost at sea;

sentences.zh: 或深入賊庭，有被傷殺。

translations.literal: some penetrating deep into the enemy camp were wounded or killed.
translations.idiomatic: some penetrating deep into enemy territory were wounded or killed.

sentences.zh: 軍法嚴重，皆須相傔。

translations.literal: Military law is severe: all must keep together.
translations.idiomatic: Military law is strict: soldiers must keep together.

sentences.zh: 若不及傔，及不因戰亡，即同隊之人，兼合有罪。

translations.literal: If one fails to keep together, or dies other than in battle, the men of the same squad are also guilty.
translations.idiomatic: If a man fails to keep with his unit or dies other than in battle, his squad mates are also guilty.

sentences.zh: 遂有無故死失，多注為逃。

translations.literal: Thus there are deaths and disappearances without cause, many recorded as desertions.
translations.idiomatic: Thus many deaths and disappearances are wrongly recorded as desertions.

sentences.zh: 軍旅之中，不暇勘當，直據隊司通狀，將作真逃，家口令總沒官，論情實可哀湣。

translations.literal: In the army there is no time for investigation; relying directly on the squad leader's general report, they are treated as true deserters and the households ordered wholly confiscated—in reason this is truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: In the field there is no time for investigation; squad reports alone mark men as deserters and their families for confiscation—a truly pitiable situation.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：‘與其殺不辜，寧失不經。

translations.literal: The Documents say: 'Better to err by not executing the guilty than to kill the innocent.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: 'Better to spare the guilty than execute the innocent.'

sentences.zh: ’伏願逃亡之家，免其配沒。

translations.literal: ' I humbly beg that the households of deserters be spared confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the families of deserters be spared confiscation.

sentences.zh: ”製從之。

translations.literal: " The edict followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 咸亨二年，駕幸東都，留太子於京師監國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianheng the emperor visited the Eastern Capital and left the crown prince in the capital to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: In 671 the emperor went to Luoyang and left the crown prince in Chang'an to oversee the state.

sentences.zh: 時屬大旱，關中饑乏，令取廓下兵士糧視之，見有食榆皮蓬實者，乃令家令等各給米使足。

translations.literal: At that time there was severe drought; Guanzhong suffered famine. He ordered the grain rations of soldiers under the palace examined and saw some eating elm bark and cattail seeds; he then ordered the household directors and others each to supply rice until they had enough.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought had brought famine to Guanzhong. He inspected soldiers' rations and found men eating elm bark and cattail seeds; he ordered the palace staff to supply them with sufficient rice.

sentences.zh: 是時戴至德、張文瓘兼左庶子，與右庶子蕭德昭同為輔弼，太子多疾病，庶政皆決於至德等。

translations.literal: At that time Dai Zhide and Zhang Wenguan concurrently served as Left Vice Directors of the Crown Prince's Household, and with Right Vice Director Xiao Dezhao jointly assisted him; the crown prince was often ill, and routine affairs were all decided by Zhide and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhide and Zhang Wenguan served as Left Vice Directors, with Xiao Dezhao as Right Vice Director. The crown prince was often ill, and routine affairs were decided by them.

sentences.zh: 時義陽、宣城二公主以母得罪，幽於掖庭，太子見之驚惻，遽奏請令出降。

translations.literal: At that time the two princesses of Yiyang and Xuancheng, because their mother had been punished, were confined in the rear palace; when the crown prince saw them he was struck with pity and hastily memorialized requesting that they be allowed to marry.
translations.idiomatic: The princesses of Yiyang and Xuancheng, whose mother had been punished, were confined in the rear palace. The crown prince was moved with pity and memorialized that they be allowed to marry.

sentences.zh: 又請以同州沙苑地分借貧人。

translations.literal: He also requested that land in Shayuan, Tongzhou, be lent in parcels to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that land in Shayuan, Tongzhou, be lent to the poor.

sentences.zh: 詔並許之。

translations.literal: Edicts approved both requests.
translations.idiomatic: Both requests were approved.

sentences.zh: 又召詣東都，納右衛將軍裴居道女為妃。

translations.literal: He was again summoned to the Eastern Capital and took as consort the daughter of Right Guards General Pei Judao.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to Luoyang and took as consort the daughter of Right Guards General Pei Judao.

sentences.zh: 所司奏以白雁為贄，適會苑中獲白雁，高宗喜曰：“漢獲朱雁，遂為樂府；

translations.literal: The responsible offices reported that a white goose would serve as betrothal gift; it happened that a white goose was caught in the park, and Emperor Gaozong rejoiced: "When Han obtained the vermilion goose, it became a music-bureau piece;"
translations.idiomatic: The offices reported a white goose as betrothal gift, and one was caught in the imperial park. Gaozong rejoiced: "When the Han obtained a vermilion goose, it became a court song;"

sentences.zh: 今獲白雁，得為婚贄。

translations.literal: "now we have obtained a white goose and may use it as a marriage gift."
translations.idiomatic: "now we have a white goose for a marriage gift."

sentences.zh: 彼禮但成謠頌，此禮便首人倫，異代相望，我無慚德也。

translations.literal: That ritual only produced ballads of praise; this ritual heads the human relationships—ages apart yet facing each other, I have no cause for shame in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: That ritual produced only songs of praise; this one crowns the bonds of kinship. Ages apart, yet I need not blush for virtue.

sentences.zh: ”裴氏甚有婦禮，高宗嚐謂侍臣曰：“東宮內政，吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: " Lady Pei was most observant of wifely ritual; Emperor Gaozong once told his attendants: "The inner governance of the Eastern Palace—I have no worries about it."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pei was exemplary in wifely conduct. Gaozong once told his attendants: "The Eastern Palace household needs no concern from me."

sentences.zh: 上元二年，太子從幸合璧宮，尋薨，年二十四。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan the crown prince accompanied the emperor to Hebi Palace and soon died, aged twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In 675 the crown prince accompanied the emperor to Hebi Palace and soon died, aged twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 製曰：“皇太子弘，生知誕質，惟幾毓性。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Crown Prince Hong was born knowing, his nature heaven-bestowed, his disposition nurtured in subtlety."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Crown Prince Hong was born wise, his nature heaven-bestowed, his character finely nurtured."

sentences.zh: 直城趨賀，肅敬著於三朝；

translations.literal: Rushing through Zhicheng to offer congratulations, his solemn respect was manifest in the three audiences;
translations.idiomatic: His solemn respect was manifest at court audiences;

sentences.zh: 中寢問安，仁孝聞於四海。

translations.literal: inquiring after the emperor's welfare at the inner quarters, his benevolence and filial piety were known throughout the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: his filial inquiries at the inner quarters won renown throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 自琰圭在手，沉瘵嬰身，顧惟耀掌之珍，特切鍾心之念，庶其痊復，以禪鴻名。

translations.literal: From the time the ceremonial jade was in his hand, lingering illness afflicted his person; looking upon the treasure in the palm of glory, my heart's special devotion was keen, hoping he might recover to yield the great name.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he received the heir's jade, illness afflicted him. I cherished him as the treasure of my palm and hoped he would recover to receive the great succession.

sentences.zh: 及腠理微和，將遜於位，而弘天資仁厚，孝心純確，既承朕命，掩不言，因茲感結，舊疾增甚。

translations.literal: When his constitution showed slight improvement and he was about to yield the position, yet Hong's inborn nature was benevolent and thick, his filial heart pure and true—having received my command he kept silent, and because of this emotional knot his old illness grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: When he seemed to improve and was about to yield the throne, Hong's nature was so benevolent and filial that, having received my command, he kept silent; the emotional strain worsened his old illness.

sentences.zh: 億兆攸係，方崇下武之基；

translations.literal: The myriad people depended on him; we were just exalting the foundation of lower martial virtue;
translations.idiomatic: The people depended on him; we were establishing the foundation of the dynasty;

sentences.zh: 五福無徵，俄遷上賓之駕。

translations.literal: the five blessings gave no sign, and suddenly he moved to the carriage of the exalted guest.
translations.idiomatic: yet the five blessings failed, and suddenly he departed as a guest on high.

sentences.zh: 昔周文至愛，遂延慶於九齡；

translations.literal: Formerly King Wen of Zhou, in utmost love, extended his blessing to ninety years;
translations.idiomatic: King Wen of Zhou, in utmost love, was blessed with long life;

sentences.zh: 朕之不慈，遽永訣於千古。

translations.literal: my lack of kindness has hastened eternal parting for a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: but my lack of kindness has brought eternal parting.

sentences.zh: 天性之重，追懷哽咽，宜申往命，加以尊名。

translations.literal: The weight of natural affection—in recollection I choke with sobs; the former command should be carried out and an honored name added.
translations.idiomatic: The weight of paternal love moves me to tears. His former command should be fulfilled and an honored name bestowed.

sentences.zh: 夫諡者，行之跡也；

translations.literal: A posthumous name is the trace of conduct;
translations.idiomatic: A posthumous name records conduct;

sentences.zh: 號者，事之表也。

translations.literal: a title is the outward sign of deeds.
translations.idiomatic: a title is the outward sign of deeds.

sentences.zh: 慈惠愛親曰‘孝’，死不忘君曰‘敬’，諡為孝敬皇帝。

translations.literal: Benevolent and loving toward kin is called 'Xiao'; not forgetting the ruler in death is called 'Jing'—his posthumous name is Emperor Xiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolent love of kin is Xiao; not forgetting the ruler in death is Jing—his posthumous name is Emperor Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: ”其年，葬於緱氏縣景山之恭陵。

translations.literal: " That year he was buried at Gongling on Jingshan in Gouyi County.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was buried at Gongling on Jingshan in Gouyi County.

sentences.zh: 制度一準天子之禮，百官從權製三十六日降服。

translations.literal: The regulations followed the rites of the Son of Heaven in full; the hundred officials, following expedient practice, wore reduced mourning for thirty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: The rites followed those of an emperor in full; officials wore reduced mourning for thirty-six days by expedient practice.

sentences.zh: 高宗親為製《睿德紀》，並自書之於石，樹於陵側。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong personally composed the Record of Sagely Virtue and himself inscribed it on stone, setting it up beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong personally composed the Record of Sagely Virtue, inscribed it on stone, and set it beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 初，將營築恭陵，功費钜億，萬姓厭役，呼嗟滿道，遂亂投磚瓦而散。

translations.literal: When construction of Gongling was first undertaken, the labor costs ran to hundreds of millions; the people wearied of corvée, lamentations filled the roads, and they thereupon scattered in disorder, hurling bricks and tiles.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongling was first built, costs ran to hundreds of millions. The people wearied of corvée, lamentations filled the roads, and workers scattered, hurling bricks and tiles.

sentences.zh: 太子無子，長壽中，製令楚王諱繼其後。

translations.literal: The crown prince had no son; during Changshou an edict ordered Prince of Chu Hui to continue his line.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had no son; during the Changshou era an edict named Prince of Chu Hui as his heir.

sentences.zh: 中宗踐祚，製祔於太廟，號曰義宗，又追贈妃裴氏為哀皇后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, an edict enshrined him in the Grand Ancestral Temple under the title Yizong, and posthumously enfeoffed Consort Pei as Empress Ai.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne, an edict enshrined Hong in the ancestral temple as Yizong and posthumously made Consort Pei Empress Ai.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，中書令姚元之、吏部尚書宋璟奏言：“準禮，大行皇帝山陵事終，即合祔廟。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun, Chief Minister of the Secretariat Yao Yuanzhi and Minister of Personnel Song Jing memorialized: "According to ritual, when the late emperor's tomb works are finished, he should be enshrined in the temple."
translations.idiomatic: In 710 Yao Yuanzhi and Song Jing memorialized: "By ritual, when the late emperor's tomb is complete, he should be enshrined in the temple."

sentences.zh: 其太廟第七室，先祔皇昆義宗孝敬皇帝、哀皇后裴氏神主。

translations.literal: In the seventh chamber of the Grand Temple, the spirit tablets of the emperor's elder brother Yizong, Emperor Xiaojing, and Empress Ai Lady Pei had already been enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh chamber of the Grand Temple already held the tablets of Yizong, Emperor Xiaojing, and Empress Ai Lady Pei.

sentences.zh: 伏以義宗未登大位，崩後追尊，至神龍之初，乃特令升祔。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that Yizong never ascended the great position; after death he was posthumously honored, and only at the beginning of Shenlong was he specially ordered elevated to the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong never actually reigned; he was honored only after death and enshrined in the temple only at the start of the Shenlong era.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義，國君即位未逾年者，不合列昭穆。

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that a ruler who took the throne for less than a year should not be placed in the zhao-mu sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals hold that a ruler who reigned less than a year should not enter the ancestral sequence.

sentences.zh: 又古者祖宗各別立廟，孝敬皇帝恭陵既在洛州，望於東都別立義宗之廟，遷祔孝敬皇帝、哀皇后神主，命有司以時享祭，則不違先旨，又協古訓，人神允穆，進退得宜。

translations.literal: Moreover, in antiquity ancestors each had separate temples erected; since Emperor Xiaojing's Gongling is in Luozhou, we beg that a separate temple to Yizong be built in the Eastern Capital, the spirit tablets of Emperor Xiaojing and Empress Ai moved there, and the responsible offices ordered to perform seasonal sacrifices—thus not violating the former intent, also conforming to ancient teaching, spirits and men in harmony, advance and retreat proper.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity ancestors had separate temples. Since Gongling is in Luozhou, we beg that a separate temple to Yizong be built in Luoyang, the tablets of Emperor Xiaojing and Empress Ai moved there, and seasonal sacrifices ordered—honoring precedent, conforming to ancient teaching, and satisfying both spirits and men.

sentences.zh: 在此神主，望入夾室安置，伏願陛下以禮斷恩。

translations.literal: As for these spirit tablets here, we beg they be placed in the side chamber; we humbly wish Your Majesty to decide affection by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: As for the tablets here, we beg they be placed in the side chamber. We humbly wish Your Majesty to let ritual govern affection.

sentences.zh: ”詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 開元六年，有司上言：“孝敬皇帝今別廟將建，亨祔有期，準禮，不合更以義宗為廟號，請以本諡孝敬為廟稱。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaiyuan the responsible offices reported: "Emperor Xiaojing's separate temple is now to be built and the offering of enshrinement is due; according to ritual it is not proper to use Yizong again as the temple name—we beg to use his original posthumous name Xiaojing as the temple designation."
translations.idiomatic: In 718 the offices reported: "Emperor Xiaojing's separate temple is to be built. By ritual the temple should not be called Yizong but should use his posthumous name Xiaojing."

sentences.zh: ”於是始停義宗之號。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the title Yizong was first discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: The title Yizong was then discontinued.

sentences.zh: 附 裴居道

translations.literal: Appended: Pei Judao
translations.idiomatic: Appended: Pei Judao

sentences.zh: 裴居道，絳州聞喜人，隋兵部侍郎鏡民孫也。

translations.literal: Pei Judao, a native of Wenxi in Jiangzhou, was grandson of Jingmin, Vice Minister of War of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Judao, a native of Wenxi in Jiangzhou, was grandson of Jingmin, Sui Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 父熙載，貞觀中為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: His father Xizai served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs in the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xizai served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs under Taizong.

sentences.zh: 居道以女為太子妃，則天時，歷位納言、內史、太子少保，封翼國公。

translations.literal: Judao, because his daughter was crown princess, during Zetian's reign successively held the posts of Admonisher, Inner Scribe, and Junior Guardian to the Crown Prince, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Because his daughter was crown princess, during Wu Zetian's reign Judao served as Admonisher, Inner Scribe, and Junior Guardian to the Crown Prince, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yiguo.

sentences.zh: 載初元年春，為酷吏所陷，下獄死。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Zaichu he was framed by cruel officials, thrown into prison, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 689 he was framed by notorious investigators, imprisoned, and died.

sentences.zh: 章懷太子賢

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhanghuai Xian
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhanghuai Xian

sentences.zh: 上元二上，孝敬皇帝薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan, Emperor Xiaojing died.
translations.idiomatic: In 675 Emperor Xiaojing died.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，立為皇太子，大赦天下，尋令監國。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year he was established as crown prince; a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm, and soon he was ordered to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year he was named crown prince. A general amnesty was declared, and he was soon ordered to oversee the state.

sentences.zh: 賢處事明審，為時論所稱。

translations.literal: Xian was clear and discerning in handling affairs and was praised by contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was clear and discerning in affairs and won praise from his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳元年，手敕褒之曰：“皇太子賢自頃監國，留心政要。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yifeng a handwritten edict praised him: "Crown Prince Xian, since lately overseeing the state, has attended to the essentials of government."
translations.idiomatic: In 676 a handwritten edict praised him: "Crown Prince Xian, since overseeing the state, has attended to the essentials of government."

sentences.zh: 撫字之道，既盡於哀矜；

translations.literal: In the way of cherishing and nurturing, he has fully exercised compassion;
translations.idiomatic: In governing the people he has shown full compassion;

sentences.zh: 刑綱所施，務存於審察。

translations.literal: in the penal statutes he applies, he strives to preserve careful scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: in applying the law he strives for careful scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 加以聽覽餘暇，專精墳典。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the leisure left from hearing and reviewing affairs, he concentrates on the classics of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: In his leisure from state affairs he devotes himself to the classics.

sentences.zh: 往聖遺編，鹹窺壺奧；

translations.literal: the surviving writings of past sages—he has all glimpsed their inner mysteries;
translations.idiomatic: He has mastered the inner mysteries of the sages' writings;

sentences.zh: 先王策府，備討菁華。

translations.literal: the policy archives of former kings—he has fully studied their finest essence.
translations.idiomatic: and studied the finest passages in the royal archives.

sentences.zh: 好善載彰，作貞斯在，家國之寄，深副所懷。

translations.literal: His love of goodness is ever manifest, his constancy is present—the trust of family and state deeply fulfills my hopes.
translations.idiomatic: His love of virtue is manifest and his constancy proven—the hopes I place in him for family and state are fully met.

sentences.zh: 可賜物五百段。

translations.literal: He may be granted five hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him five hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: ”賢又招集當時學者太子左庶子張大安、洗馬劉訥言、洛州司戶格希玄、學士許叔牙成玄一史藏諸周寶寧等，注范曄《後漢書》，表上之，賜物三萬段，仍以其書付秘閣。

translations.literal: " Xian also gathered the scholars of the time—Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Zhang Da'an, Groom Liu Nayan, Luozhou Registrar Ge Xixuan, Academicians Xu Shuya, Cheng Xuanyi, Shi Cang, Zhu Zhou, and Bao Ning—and annotated Fan Ye's Book of Later Han, submitting a memorial with it; he was granted thirty thousand bolts of goods, and the book was deposited in the Secretariat Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Xian also gathered scholars including Zhang Da'an, Liu Nayan, Ge Xixuan, Xu Shuya, Cheng Xuanyi, and others to annotate Fan Ye's Book of Later Han. He submitted it to the throne, received thirty thousand bolts of goods, and the work was deposited in the imperial archive.

sentences.zh: 時正議大夫明崇儼以符劾之術為則天所任使，密稱“英王狀類太宗”。

translations.literal: At that time Rectifier of Discourse Ming Chongyan, skilled in talismanic investigation, was employed by Zetian and secretly said, "Prince Ying's appearance resembles Emperor Taizong."
translations.idiomatic: Ming Chongyan, a specialist in occult investigation favored by Wu Zetian, secretly said that Prince Ying resembled Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 又宮人潛議雲“賢是後姊韓國夫人所生”，賢亦自疑懼。

translations.literal: Palace women also whispered that "Xian was born to the late elder sister, Lady of Korea," and Xian himself grew suspicious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women also whispered that Xian was born to Wu's late sister, Lady of Korea, and Xian himself grew fearful.

sentences.zh: 則天又嚐為賢撰《少陽政範》及《孝子傳》以賜之，仍數作書以責讓賢，賢逾不自安。

translations.literal: Zetian also once composed the Political Standards of Lesser Yang and the Biographies of Filial Sons for Xian as gifts, yet repeatedly wrote letters reproaching him, and Xian grew ever more uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian also composed Political Standards of Lesser Yang and Biographies of Filial Sons for him, yet repeatedly wrote letters reproaching him, and Xian grew ever more uneasy.

sentences.zh: 調露二年，崇儼為盜所殺，則天疑賢所為。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiaolu, Chongyan was killed by bandits; Zetian suspected Xian was responsible.
translations.idiomatic: In 680 Chongyan was killed by bandits, and Wu Zetian suspected Xian.

sentences.zh: 俄使人發其陰謀事，詔令中書侍郎薛元超、黃門侍郎裴炎、御史大夫高智周與法官推鞫之，於東宮馬坊搜得皂甲數百領，乃廢賢為庶人，幽於別所。

translations.literal: Soon agents uncovered his conspiracy; an edict ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat Xue Yuanchao, Vice Director of the Gate-Emperor Pei Yan, Censor-in-Chief Gao Zhizhou, and judicial officials to interrogate him. In the Eastern Palace horse stable several hundred suits of black armor were found; Xian was then deposed as commoner and confined in a separate place.
translations.idiomatic: Agents soon uncovered a conspiracy. Xue Yuanchao, Pei Yan, Gao Zhizhou, and judicial officials were ordered to investigate. Hundreds of suits of black armor were found in the Eastern Palace stables. Xian was deposed as a commoner and confined.

sentences.zh: 永淳二年，遷於巴州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchun he was transferred to Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 683 he was transferred to Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 文明元年，則天臨朝，令左金吾將軍丘神勣往巴州檢校賢宅，以備外虞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wenming, when Zetian held court, she ordered Left Golden Crow General Qiu Shenji to go to Bazhou to inspect Xian's residence against external trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In 684 Wu Zetian ordered Left Golden Crow General Qiu Shenji to inspect Xian's residence at Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 神勣遂閉於別室，逼令自殺，年三十二。

translations.literal: Shenji thereupon confined him in a separate room and forced him to kill himself; he was thirty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: Shenji confined him and forced him to kill himself. He was thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 則天舉哀於顯福門，貶神勣為疊州刺史，追封賢為雍王。

translations.literal: Zetian mourned at Xianfu Gate, demoted Shenji to Prefect of Diezhou, and posthumously enfeoffed Xian as Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian mourned at Xianfu Gate, demoted Shenji to Prefect of Diezhou, and posthumously enfeoffed Xian as Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追贈司徒，仍遣使迎其喪柩，陪葬於乾陵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was posthumously made Minister of Education; envoys were still sent to bring back his coffin, and he was buried beside Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era he was posthumously made Minister of Education, his coffin brought back, and he was buried beside Qianling.

sentences.zh: 睿宗踐祚，又追贈皇太子，諡曰章懷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he was further posthumously made crown prince, with the posthumous name Zhanghuai.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, Xian was posthumously made crown prince with the name Zhanghuai.

sentences.zh: 有三子：光順、守禮、守義。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Guangshun, Shouli, and Shouyi.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Guangshun, Shouli, and Shouyi.

sentences.zh: 光順，大授中封安樂郡王，尋被誅。

translations.literal: Guangshun, in the Dashou era was enfeoffed as Prince of Anle commandery and soon was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshun was enfeoffed as Prince of Anle during the Dashou era and was soon executed.

sentences.zh: 守義，文明年封犍為郡王。

translations.literal: Shouyi, in the Wenming era was enfeoffed as Prince of Jianwei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi was enfeoffed as Prince of Jianwei in the Wenming era.

sentences.zh: 垂拱四年，徙封永安郡王，病卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chuigong his title was changed to Prince of Yong'an commandery; he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 688 he was transferred to Prince of Yong'an and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 守禮本名光仁，垂拱初改名守禮，授太子洗馬，封嗣雍王。

translations.literal: Shouli's original name was Guangren; at the beginning of Chuigong he was renamed Shouli, appointed Crown Prince Groom, and enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Shouli, originally named Guangren, was renamed Shouli early in the Chuigong era, appointed Crown Prince Groom, and enfeoffed as heir to the Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 時中宗遷於房陵，睿宗雖居帝位，絕人朝謁，諸武讚成革命之計，深嫉宗枝。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongzong was moved to Fangling; although Ruizong occupied the imperial position, no one came to court audience; the Wu clan praised and accomplished the plan for dynastic change and deeply resented the imperial clan branches.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong had been sent to Fangling. Ruizong held the throne but received no court audiences. The Wu clan promoted Wu Zetian's takeover and deeply resented the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 守禮以父得罪，與睿宗諸子同處於宮中，凡十餘年不出庭院。

translations.literal: Because his father had offended, Shouli dwelt together with Ruizong's sons inside the palace—for more than ten years he did not leave the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had been disgraced, Shouli lived in the palace with Ruizong's sons and did not leave the courtyard for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 至聖曆元年，睿宗自皇嗣封為相王，許出外邸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenli, Ruizong was enfeoffed from Imperial Heir as Prince of Xiang and permitted a residence outside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In 698 Ruizong was enfeoffed from Imperial Heir as Prince of Xiang and allowed to live outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 睿宗諸子五子皆封郡王，與守禮始居於外。

translations.literal: All five of Ruizong's sons were enfeoffed as commandery princes; Shouli began living outside together with them.
translations.idiomatic: All five of Ruizong's sons were enfeoffed as commandery princes, and Shouli began living outside the palace with them.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，中宗纂位，授守禮光祿卿同正員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, when Zhongzong succeeded the throne, Shouli was appointed Commissioner of the Imperial Household with concurrent regular status.
translations.idiomatic: In 705, when Zhongzong took the throne, Shouli was appointed Commissioner of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，遺詔進封邠王，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: During Shenlong, by testamentary edict he was advanced to Prince of Bin and granted five hundred households of substantive enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era a testamentary edict advanced him to Prince of Bin and granted five hundred households of substantive enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，帶光祿卿，兼幽州刺史，轉左金吾衛大將軍，遙領單於大都護。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun he held the title of Commissioner of the Imperial Household concurrently, also served as Prefect of Youzhou, was transferred to Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard, and nominally held the post of Grand Protector of the Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: In 711 he served concurrently as Commissioner of the Imperial Household and Prefect of Youzhou, then became Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard and nominal Grand Protector of the Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 先天二年，遷司空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiantian he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 713 he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 開元初，歷虢、隴、襄、晉、滑六州刺史，非奏事及大事，並上佐知州。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan he successively served as prefect of the six prefectures Guo, Long, Xiang, Jin, and Hua; except for memorial audiences and major affairs, the senior assistants managed prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he served successively as prefect of Guo, Long, Xiang, Jin, and Hua. Except for audiences and major matters, senior assistants ran the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時寧、申、岐、薛、邠同為刺史，皆擇首僚以持綱紀。

translations.literal: At that time the princes Ning, Shen, Qi, Xue, and Bin alike served as prefects; each chose leading staff to uphold regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The princes Ning, Shen, Qi, Xue, and Bin all served as prefects at the time, each choosing capable senior staff to maintain order.

sentences.zh: 源乾曜、袁嘉祚、潘好禮皆為邠府長史兼州佐，守禮唯弋獵、伎樂、飲謔而已。

translations.literal: Yuan Qianyao, Yuan Jiazuo, and Pan Haoli all served as chief secretary of the Bin princely establishment and concurrent prefectural assistant; Shouli devoted himself only to hunting, music, and drinking banter.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qianyao, Yuan Jiazuo, and Pan Haoli served as chief secretary of the Bin establishment and prefectural assistants, while Shouli spent his time only on hunting, music, and carousing.

sentences.zh: 九年已後，諸王並征還京師。

translations.literal: After the ninth year all princes were recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After the ninth year all princes were recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 賢子邠王 守禮

translations.literal: Sons of Xian: Prince of Bin, Shouli
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Xian: Prince of Bin, Shouli

sentences.zh: 守禮以外枝為王，才識猥下，尤不逮岐、薛。

translations.literal: As a collateral-branch prince, his talent and knowledge were low, especially not reaching the level of Qi and Xue.
translations.idiomatic: As a prince of collateral descent, his talent was poor and fell far short of the princes Qi and Xue.

sentences.zh: 多寵嬖，不修風教，男女六十餘人，男無中才，女負貞稱，守禮居之自若，高歌擊鼓。

translations.literal: He had many favored concubines and did not cultivate moral teaching; he had more than sixty sons and daughters—the men had no middling talent, the women bore reputations for chastity—yet Shouli dwelt at ease, singing loudly and beating drums.
translations.idiomatic: He kept many concubines and neglected moral instruction. He had more than sixty children—the sons showed no middling ability, the daughters were praised for chastity—yet Shouli lived at ease, singing and beating drums.

sentences.zh: 常帶數千貫錢債，或有諫之者曰：“王年漸高，家累甚眾，須有愛惜。

translations.literal: He constantly carried debts of several thousand strings of cash; someone who remonstrated with him said, "Your Highness's years are gradually advanced, household burdens are very numerous—you must be sparing."
translations.idiomatic: He was always thousands of strings in debt. Someone advised him, "Your Highness is growing older and your household is large—you must be more careful with money."

sentences.zh: ”守禮曰：“豈有天子兄沒人葬？

translations.literal: " Shouli said, "How could there be the Son of Heaven's elder brother with no one to bury him?"
translations.idiomatic: Shouli replied, "How could the emperor's elder brother have no one to bury him?"

sentences.zh: ”諸王因內宴言之，以為歡笑。

translations.literal: " The princes spoke of this at an inner banquet and took it as amusement.
translations.idiomatic: The princes retold this at an inner banquet and found it hilarious.

sentences.zh: 時積陰累日，守禮白於諸王曰：“欲晴。

translations.literal: When cloudy weather had accumulated for many days, Shouli announced to the princes, "It will clear."
translations.idiomatic: When clouds had lingered for days, Shouli told the princes, "It will clear up."

sentences.zh: ”果晴。

translations.literal: " It did clear.
translations.idiomatic: It did clear.

sentences.zh: 愆陽涉旬，守禮曰：“即雨。

translations.literal: When drought lasted more than ten days, Shouli said, "It will rain soon."
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days of drought, Shouli said, "It will rain soon."

sentences.zh: ”果連澍。

translations.literal: " Rain indeed fell continuously.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell steadily.

sentences.zh: 岐王等奏之，云：“邠哥有術。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi and others reported to the throne, saying, "Brother Bin has arts."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi and others reported that "Brother Bin" had occult skill.

sentences.zh: ”守禮曰：“臣無術也。

translations.literal: " Shouli said, "Your subject has no arts."
translations.idiomatic: Shouli said, "I have no such skill."

sentences.zh: 則天時以章懷遷謫，臣幽閉宮中十餘年，每歲被敕杖數頓，見瘢痕甚厚。

translations.literal: In Wu Zetian's time, because Zhanghuai was demoted and banished, I was confined in the palace more than ten years; each year I was ordered beaten several times—I saw scars very thick.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu Zetian's reign, when Zhanghuai was banished, I was confined in the palace for more than ten years. Each year I was ordered beaten several times, and the scars on my back are very thick.

sentences.zh: 欲雨，臣脊上即沉悶，欲晴，即輕健，臣以此知之，非有術也。

translations.literal: When rain was coming, my back would at once feel heavy and dull; when clear weather was coming, it would feel light and agile—I knew by this; I have no arts.
translations.idiomatic: When rain was coming my back felt heavy and dull; when fair weather was coming it felt light and agile. I knew from that—I have no occult skill.

sentences.zh: ”涕泗沾襟，玄宗亦憫然。

translations.literal: " Tears and mucus soaked his collar; Emperor Xuanzong also felt compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Tears soaked his robe, and Emperor Xuanzong was moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 二十九年薨，年七十餘，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died; he was over seventy years old and was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his twenty-ninth year of office, aged over seventy, and was posthumously made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 子 承宏

translations.literal: Son Chenghong
translations.idiomatic: Son Chenghong

sentences.zh: 子承宏，開元初封廣武郡王，歷秘書員外監，又為宗正卿同正員。

translations.literal: His son Chenghong, early in Kaiyuan was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangwu commandery, served successively as superintendent of the Secretariat as supplementary appointee, and also as Director of the Imperial Clan with concurrent regular status.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chenghong was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangwu early in Kaiyuan, served as superintendent of the Secretariat, and later as Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，吐蕃淩犯上都，乘輿幸陝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde the Tibetans invaded and raided the upper capital; the imperial carriage went to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: In 763 Tibetans raided the capital and the emperor went to Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 蕃、渾之眾入城，吐蕃宰相馬重英立承宏為帝，以於可封、霍環等為宰相，補署百餘人。

translations.literal: Tibetan and Hun forces entered the city; Tibetan minister Ma Chongying installed Chenghong as emperor, made Yu Kefeng, Huo Huan, and others chancellors, and supplemented appointments for more than a hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan and Hun troops entered the city. The Tibetan minister Ma Chongying installed Chenghong as emperor, appointed Yu Kefeng and Huo Huan as chancellors, and filled more than a hundred posts.

sentences.zh: 旬餘日，賊退，郭子儀率眾入城，送承宏於行在，上不之責，止於虢州。

translations.literal: After more than ten days the bandits retreated; Guo Ziyi led troops into the city and sent Chenghong to the mobile court; the emperor did not blame him and confined him to Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days the enemy withdrew. Guo Ziyi entered the city and sent Chenghong to the emperor's camp. The emperor did not punish him but confined him to Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 尋死。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 承寧，天寶初，授率更令同正員，嗣邠王。

translations.literal: Chenning, early in Tianbao was appointed Director of the Imperial Workshops with concurrent regular status and succeeded as Prince of Bin.
