translations.idiomatic: Chenning, early in the Tianbao era, was appointed Director of the Imperial Workshops and succeeded as Prince of Bin.

sentences.zh: 承寀，至德二載，敦封為煌郡王，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Chenbao, in the second year of Zhide was solemnly enfeoffed as Prince of Huang commandery and given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Entitlement Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Chenbao was solemnly enfeoffed as Prince of Huang in 757 and given the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Entitlement Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 與仆固懷恩使回紇和親，因納其女為妃，冊為毗伽公主。

translations.literal: With Pugu Huai'en he was envoy for marriage alliance with the Uyghurs; he took their princess as consort and she was enfeoffed as Princess Pijia.
translations.idiomatic: With Pugu Huai'en he went as envoy to ally with the Uyghurs by marriage, took the khan's daughter as consort, and she was enfeoffed as Princess Pijia.

sentences.zh: 回紇著勳，承寀甚遇恩寵。

translations.literal: When the Uyghurs rendered meritorious service, Chenbao received very great favor and grace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghurs rendered distinguished service, Chenbao received exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年六月卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Qianyuan he died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of 758 and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 唐法，嗣郡王但加四品階，親王子例著緋。

translations.literal: Under Tang law, successor commandery princes received only a promotion of four ranks; sons of the emperor by regulation wore scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang law, heirs to commandery princely titles gained only four ranks in promotion, while sons of the emperor normally wore scarlet robes.

sentences.zh: 開元中，張九齡為中書令，奏請寧、薛王男並賜紫，邠王三男衣紫，餘二十人衣緋，官亦不越六局郎，王府掾屬仍員外置。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan, Zhang Jiuling was Secretariat Director; he memorialized requesting the sons of the Princes of Ning and Xue all be granted purple, the three sons of the Prince of Bin wear purple, the remaining twenty wear scarlet, offices not exceeding bureau directors of the six ministries, and princely staff still placed as supplementary appointees.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, Secretariat Director Zhang Jiuling memorialized that the sons of the princes Ning and Xue should all wear purple, the three sons of Prince Bin wear purple, the other twenty wear scarlet, offices not exceed bureau directors, and princely staff remain supplementary appointees.

sentences.zh: 十五載，扈從至巴蜀，依例著紫。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed in attendance to Ba-Shu and by regulation wore purple.
translations.idiomatic: In 756 he followed the emperor to Ba-Shu and wore purple by regulation.

sentences.zh: 中宗諸子

translations.literal: Sons of Zhongzong
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Zhongzong

sentences.zh: 中宗四男：章庶人生懿德太子重潤，後宮生庶人重福、節湣太子重俊、殤帝重茂。

translations.literal: Zhongzong had four sons: Lady Zhang the concubine bore the Yide heir apparent Chongrun; the rear palace bore the commoner Chongfu, the Jiemin heir apparent Chongjun, and the short-lived emperor Chongmao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong had four sons: Consort Zhang bore the Yide heir apparent Chongrun; the rear palace bore Chongfu the commoner, Chongjun the Jiemin heir apparent, and Chongmao the short-lived emperor.

sentences.zh: 懿德太子 重潤

translations.literal: Yide Heir Apparent Chongrun
translations.idiomatic: Yide Heir Apparent Chongrun

sentences.zh: 懿德太子重潤，中宗長子也。

translations.literal: Yide Heir Apparent Chongrun was Zhongzong's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Yide Heir Apparent Chongrun was Zhongzong's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 本名重照，以避則天諱，故改焉。

translations.literal: His original name was Chongzhao; to avoid Wu Zetian's taboo it was therefore changed.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Chongzhao; it was changed to avoid Wu Zetian's taboo name.

sentences.zh: 開耀二年，中宗為皇太子，生重潤於東宮內殿，高宗甚悅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyao, when Zhongzong was crown prince, Chongrun was born in the eastern palace inner hall; Emperor Gaozong was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In 682, while Zhongzong was crown prince, Chongrun was born in the Eastern Palace. Emperor Gaozong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 及月滿，大赦天下，改元為永淳。

translations.literal: When the month was complete, a great amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven and the era name changed to Yongchun.
translations.idiomatic: When the month was complete, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Yongchun.

sentences.zh: 是歲，立為皇太孫，開府置官屬。

translations.literal: That year he was installed as Imperial Great-Grandson and an office was established with officials.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was installed as imperial great-grandson and a staff office was established.

sentences.zh: 及中宗遷於房州，其府坐廢。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was moved to Fangzhou, his establishment was abolished for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was sent to Fangzhou, the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 聖曆初，中宗為皇太子，封為邵王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenli, when Zhongzong was crown prince, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenli era, when Zhongzong was crown prince again, Chongrun was enfeoffed as Prince of Shao.

sentences.zh: 大足元年，為人所構，與其妹永泰郡主、婿魏王武延基等竊議張易之兄弟何得恣入宮中，則天令杖殺，時年十九。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazu he was framed by others; with his younger sister Princess Yongtai, son-in-law Prince of Wei Wu Yanji, and others he privately discussed how the Zhang Yizhi brothers could roam freely into the palace—Wu Zetian ordered him beaten to death; he was nineteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: In 701 he was framed. He had privately discussed with his sister Princess Yongtai, her husband Prince of Wei Wu Yanji, and others how the Zhang brothers could enter the palace at will. Wu Zetian ordered him beaten to death. He was nineteen.

sentences.zh: 重潤風神俊朗，早以孝友知名，既死非其罪，大為當時所悼惜。

translations.literal: Chongrun's bearing was handsome and bright; early he was known for filiality and friendship; since his death was not his crime, people of the time greatly mourned and pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrun was handsome and distinguished, known early for filial piety and brotherly affection. His death was widely seen as unjust, and his contemporaries deeply mourned him.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，追贈皇太子，諡曰懿德，陪葬乾陵。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, he was posthumously made crown prince, posthumous name Yide, and buried beside Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne, Chongrun was posthumously made crown prince with the posthumous name Yide and buried beside Qianling.

sentences.zh: 仍為聘國子監丞裴粹亡女為冥婚，與之合葬。

translations.literal: He also arranged a ghost marriage with the deceased daughter of Guozijian Vice Director Pei Cui and buried them together.
translations.idiomatic: He also arranged a posthumous marriage for Chongrun with the deceased daughter of Guozijian Vice Director Pei Cui, and they were buried together.

sentences.zh: 又贈永泰郡主為公主，令備禮改葬，仍號其墓為陵焉。

translations.literal: He also posthumously made Princess Yongtai a full princess, ordered proper rites for reburial, and still titled her tomb a mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He also posthumously elevated Princess Yongtai to full princess rank, ordered a proper reburial, and designated her tomb a mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 庶人 重福

translations.literal: Commoner Chongfu
translations.idiomatic: Commoner Chongfu

sentences.zh: 庶人重福，中宗第二子也。

translations.literal: Commoner Chongfu was Zhongzong's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Commoner Chongfu was Zhongzong's second son.

sentences.zh: 初封唐昌王，聖曆三年，徙封平恩王。

translations.literal: Initially he was enfeoffed as Prince of Tangchang; in the third year of Shenli his title was changed to Prince of Ping'en.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Tangchang, then transferred to Prince of Ping'en in the third year of Shenli.

sentences.zh: 長安四年，進封譙王，歷遷國子祭酒、左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chang'an he was advanced to Prince of Qiao and successively promoted Minister of the Imperial Academy and Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In 704 he was advanced to Prince of Qiao and served successively as Minister of the Imperial Academy and Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，為韋庶人所譖，雲與張易之兄弟潛構成重潤之罪，由是左授濮州員外刺史，轉均州，司防守，不許視事。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong he was slandered by Consort Wei, saying he and the Zhang Yizhi brothers secretly framed Chongrun's crime; thereby he was demoted to supplementary prefect of Pu, transferred to Jun, served as administrative defender, and was not permitted to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era Consort Wei slandered him, claiming he and the Zhang brothers had secretly framed Chongrun. He was demoted to supplementary prefect of Pu, then transferred to Jun as administrative defender and barred from conducting office business.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，中宗親祀南郊，大赦天下，流人並放還。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jinglong, Zhongzong personally sacrificed at the southern suburb, proclaimed a great amnesty for all under Heaven, and exiles were all released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In 709 Zhongzong personally sacrificed at the southern suburb, proclaimed a general amnesty, and all exiles were released and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 重福不得歸京師，尤深鬱怏，上表自陳曰：“臣聞功同賞異，則勞臣疑；

translations.literal: Chongfu was not permitted to return to the capital and was especially deeply depressed and resentful; he submitted a memorial stating his case, saying, "Your subject has heard that when merit is the same but rewards differ, then diligent ministers grow doubtful;"
translations.idiomatic: Chongfu was not allowed to return to the capital and grew deeply resentful. He submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard that when merit is equal but rewards differ, loyal servants become doubtful;"

sentences.zh: 罪均刑殊，則百姓惑。

translations.literal: when crimes are equal but punishments differ, then the common people are perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: when crimes are equal but punishments differ, the people are perplexed;

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下德侔造化，明齊日月，恩及飛鳥，惠加走獸。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's virtue equals creation and transformation, your brilliance matches sun and moon, your grace reaches flying birds, your kindness extends to running beasts.
translations.idiomatic: your virtue equals heaven and earth, your wisdom matches the sun and moon, your grace reaches even birds in flight and beasts on the ground.

sentences.zh: 近者焚柴展禮，郊祀上玄，萬物沾愷悌之仁，六合承曠蕩之澤。

translations.literal: Recently you burned firewood and displayed the rites, sacrificing at the suburban altar to the Supreme Mystery—all things were moistened by benevolent and gentle humanity, the six directions received vast and open favor.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, at the suburban sacrifice to heaven, all things received your benevolence and the realm your boundless grace.

sentences.zh: 事無輕重，鹹赦除之。

translations.literal: Matters without regard to light or heavy—all were pardoned and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Offenses great and small were alike pardoned.

sentences.zh: 蒼生並得赦除，赤子偏加擯棄，皇天平分之道，固此乎？

translations.literal: The living masses all received pardon and removal, yet this loyal son alone was especially cast aside and abandoned—is this indeed the Way of imperial heaven's even division?
translations.idiomatic: All the people were pardoned, yet I alone am cast aside—is this the even justice of heaven?

sentences.zh: 天下之人，聞者為臣流涕。

translations.literal: People throughout the realm, hearing of it, wept tears for your subject.
translations.idiomatic: All who hear of my case weep for me.

sentences.zh: 況陛下慈念，豈不湣臣恓惶？

translations.literal: How much more should Your Majesty's compassionate thoughts not pity your subject's distress and anxiety?
translations.idiomatic: Surely Your Majesty's compassion will pity my anguish?

sentences.zh: 伏望舍臣罪愆，許臣朝謁。

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will set aside your subject's offenses and faults and permit your subject a court audience.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to overlook my faults and permit me an audience at court.

sentences.zh: 儻得一仰雲陛，再睹陛聖顏，雖沒九泉，實為萬足。

translations.literal: If I might once look up at the cloud steps and again behold Your Majesty's sage countenance, though I sink into the nine springs it would truly be more than enough.
translations.idiomatic: If I might once behold your sacred face, death itself would be more than enough reward.

sentences.zh: 重投荒徼，亦所甘心。

translations.literal: To be cast again into the remote borderlands would also be what I accept willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Even to be sent again to the frontier I would accept willingly."

sentences.zh: ”表奏不報。

translations.literal: "The memorial received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial received no response.

sentences.zh: 王道始至東都，俄有泄其謀者，洛州司馬崔日知捕獲其黨數十人。

translations.literal: When Wang Dao first arrived at the eastern capital, soon someone leaked his plot; Luozhou Vice Prefect Cui Rizhi captured several dozen of his party.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dao first reached the eastern capital, his plot was soon leaked. Luozhou Vice Prefect Cui Rizhi captured several dozen conspirators.

sentences.zh: 經聞重福至，王道等率眾隨重福徑取左右屯營兵作亂，將至天津橋，願從者已數百人，皆執持器仗，助其威勢。

translations.literal: Having heard that Chongfu had arrived, Wang Dao and others led their followers with Chongfu to take the Left and Right Garrison troops directly and raise a rebellion; when they reached Tianjin Bridge, those willing to follow already numbered several hundred, all holding weapons to augment his imposing force.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Chongfu had arrived, Wang Dao and others led followers with him to seize the Left and Right Garrison troops and rebel. Near Tianjin Bridge their party already numbered several hundred, all armed to bolster his strength.

sentences.zh: 侍御史李邕先詣左掖門，令閉關拒守。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Li Yong first went to the Left Flank Gate and ordered the gates closed to resist and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Li Yong went first to the Left Flank Gate and ordered it shut for defense.

sentences.zh: 又至右屯營號令云：“重福雖先帝之子，已得罪於先帝，今者無故入城，必是作亂。

translations.literal: He then went to the Right Garrison Camp and proclaimed, "Although Chongfu is the late emperor's son, he has already offended the late emperor; now he enters the city without cause—he must be raising a rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: He then went to the Right Garrison Camp and announced, "Chongfu may be the late emperor's son, but he already offended the late emperor. Entering the city without cause, he must be rebelling."

sentences.zh: 君等皆委質聖朝，宜盡誠節，立功立事，以取富貴。

translations.literal: You have all entrusted yourselves to the sacred court; you ought to fulfill loyal integrity, establish merit and achievement, and thereby obtain wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: You have all pledged yourselves to the dynasty. Show loyal devotion, win merit, and gain reward and rank.

sentences.zh: ”有頃，重福果來奪右屯營，堅壁不動，營中矢射如雨。

translations.literal: " Before long Chongfu indeed came to seize the Right Garrison Camp; they held the walls and did not move, while arrows from the camp fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chongfu came to attack the Right Garrison Camp. The defenders held the walls and rained arrows down on them.

sentences.zh: 便趣大臣掖門，擬取留守，遇門閉，遂縱火以燒城門。

translations.literal: He then hastened to the Great Ministers' Flank Gate, intending to seize the acting commander; finding the gate closed, he thereupon set fire to burn the city gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then rushed to the Great Ministers' Flank Gate to seize the acting commander. The gate was closed, so he set fire to burn it down.

sentences.zh: 左屯營兵又來逼之，重福度數窮，出自上東門而遁，匿於山谷間。

translations.literal: Left Garrison troops came pressing him again; Chongfu saw his resources exhausted, went out through the Upper East Gate and fled, hiding among valleys and hills.
translations.idiomatic: Left Garrison troops pressed him again. Seeing no way out, Chongfu fled through the Upper East Gate and hid in the hills.

sentences.zh: 明日，東都留守裴談等大出兵搜索，重福窘迫，自投漕河而死，磔屍三日，時年三十一。

translations.literal: The next day Eastern Capital acting commander Pei Tan and others led great forces in search; Chongfu, hard pressed, threw himself into the Transport Canal and died; his corpse was dismembered and exposed for three days; he was thirty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Eastern Capital commander Pei Tan and others searched in force. Hard pressed, Chongfu drowned himself in the canal. His corpse was dismembered and exposed for three days. He was thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：“集州刺史譙王重福，幼則凶頑，長而險詖。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Prince of Qiao Chongfu, Prefect of Jizhou, was vicious and stubborn in youth and treacherous and perverse in maturity."
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated, "Prince of Qiao Chongfu, Prefect of Jizhou, was vicious in youth and treacherous in manhood."

sentences.zh: 幸托體於先聖，嚐通交於巨逆。

translations.literal: Fortunate to receive his body from the former sage, he once associated with great traitors.
translations.idiomatic: Born of the late emperor, he once consorted with great traitors.

sentences.zh: 子而不子，自絕於天；

translations.literal: a son who was no son, cutting himself off from Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: A son who was no son, cutting himself off from Heaven;

sentences.zh: 有國有家，莫容於代。

translations.literal: with state and clan, nowhere could he be contained in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: unfit for family or state in his own age.

sentences.zh: 往者頗不含忍，長令幽縶。

translations.literal: In the past I was rather lacking in forbearance and long kept him confined.
translations.idiomatic: In the past I lacked forbearance and kept him confined long.

sentences.zh: 自大行晏駕，韋氏臨朝，將肆屠滅，尤加防衛。

translations.literal: From the time the late emperor passed away and the Wei clan held court, they were about to slaughter and destroy him, and especially increased his guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the late emperor's death the Wei clan held power and would have destroyed him, so his guard was tightened.

sentences.zh: 洎天有成命，集於朕躬，永懷猶子之情，庶協先親之義。

translations.literal: When Heaven's mandate was fulfilled and gathered upon my person, I ever cherished a nephew's affection, hoping to accord with the former kin's righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven's mandate fell to me, I cherished him as a nephew and hoped to honor my late brother's bond.

sentences.zh: 所以開置僚屬，任隆刺舉，冀其悛改，以怙恩榮。

translations.literal: Therefore I established staff for him and entrusted him with weighty investigative duties, hoping he would reform and rely on grace and glory.
translations.idiomatic: I gave him a staff and a weighty prefectural post, hoping he would reform and enjoy imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 而詿誤有徒，狂狡未息。

translations.literal: Yet there were deluded followers, and his wild cunning did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet deluded followers remained and his reckless cunning did not cease.

sentences.zh: 便即私出均州，詐乘驛騎，至於都下，遂逞其謀。

translations.literal: He thereupon left Junzhou in secret, falsely used post-station mounts, reached the capital, and then carried out his plot.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly left Junzhou, seized post horses, reached the capital, and carried out his plot.

sentences.zh: 先犯屯兵，次燒左掖，計窮力屈，投河而斃。

translations.literal: First he attacked the garrison troops, then burned the Left Flank Gate; his plans exhausted and strength spent, he cast himself into the river and perished.
translations.idiomatic: He first attacked the garrisons, then burned the Left Flank Gate. His plans failed and strength spent, he drowned himself in the river.

sentences.zh: 雖人所共棄，邦有常刑，我非不慈，爾自招咎。

translations.literal: Although all men cast him aside and the state has constant punishments, it is not that I am without kindness—you brought calamity on yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Though all men cast him off and the state has fixed punishments, I was not unkind—he brought ruin on himself.

sentences.zh: 且聞其故，有惻於懷。

translations.literal: Yet hearing the full account, compassion stirs in my breast.
translations.idiomatic: Yet hearing the full story, I am moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 昔劉長既歿，楚英遂殞，以禮收葬，抑惟舊章，屈法申恩，宜仍舊寵。

translations.literal: In former times when Liu Chang had died, Chu Ying then perished—they were buried with rites, restrained only by old statutes; bending the law to extend grace, former favor ought still to apply.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chang died and Chu Ying followed, they were buried with rites under old precedent. Bending the law to show grace, former favor should still apply.

sentences.zh: 可以三品禮葬。

translations.literal: He may be buried with third-rank rites."
translations.idiomatic: He may be buried with third-rank rites."

sentences.zh: 節湣太子 重俊

translations.literal: Jiemin Heir Apparent Chongjun
translations.idiomatic: Jiemin Heir Apparent Chongjun

sentences.zh: 時武三思得幸中宮，深忌重俊。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Sansi had gained favor in the inner palace and deeply resented Chongjun.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Sansi had the empress's favor and deeply resented Chongjun.

sentences.zh: 三思子崇訓尚安樂公主，常教公主淩忽重俊，以其非韋氏所生，常呼之為奴。

translations.literal: Sansi's son Chongxun married Princess Anle and often taught the princess to humiliate Chongjun; because he was not born of the Wei clan, they often called him a slave.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi's son Chongxun married Princess Anle and often urged her to humiliate Chongjun. Because he was not born of Empress Wei, they called him a slave.

sentences.zh: 或勸公主請廢重俊為王，自立為皇太女，重俊不勝忿恨。

translations.literal: Some urged the princess to request that Chongjun be demoted to prince and that she herself be installed as imperial great-daughter; Chongjun could not bear the rage.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged the princess to have Chongjun demoted to prince and make herself heir as "imperial great-daughter." Chongjun was consumed with hatred.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，率左羽林大將軍李多祚、右羽林將軍李思衝、李承況、獨孤禕之、沙吒忠義等，矯製發左右羽林兵及千騎三百餘人，殺三思及崇訓於其第，並殺黨與十餘人。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year he led Left Feathered Forest Grand General Li Duozuo, Right Feathered Forest General Li Sichong, Li Chengkang, Dugu Yizhi, Shazha Zhongyi, and others; by forged edict he mobilized Left and Right Feathered Forest troops and more than three hundred of the Thousand Riders, killed Sansi and Chongxun at their residence, and also killed more than ten of their party.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 707 he led Li Duozuo, Li Sichong, Li Chengkang, Dugu Yizhi, Shazha Zhongyi, and others. By forged edict he mobilized the Left and Right Feathered Forest guards and over three hundred Thousand Riders, killed Sansi and Chongxun at their mansion, and slew more than ten accomplices.

sentences.zh: 又令左金吾大將軍成王千里分兵守宮城諸門，自率兵趨肅章門，斬關而入，求韋庶人及安樂公主所在。

translations.literal: He also ordered Left Golden Crow Grand General Prince of Cheng Li Qianli to divide forces and guard the palace-city gates; he himself led troops to Su Zhang Gate, cut through the barrier and entered, seeking where Consort Wei and Princess Anle were.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Prince of Cheng Li Qianli to hold the palace gates with divided forces while he led troops to Su Zhang Gate, broke through, and searched for Consort Wei and Princess Anle.

sentences.zh: 又以昭容上官氏素與三思奸通，扣閤索之。

translations.literal: Because Shangguan the Brilliant Consort had long had illicit relations with Sansi, he also knocked on doors seeking her.
translations.idiomatic: He also sought out Brilliant Consort Shangguan, who had long been Sansi's lover.

sentences.zh: 韋庶人及公主遽擁帝馳赴玄武門樓，召左羽林將軍劉仁景等，令率留軍飛騎及百餘人於樓下列守。

translations.literal: Consort Wei and the princess hastily embraced the emperor and galloped to Xuánwu Gate tower; they summoned Left Feathered Forest General Liu Renjing and others and ordered them to lead the remaining Flying Cavalry and more than a hundred men to guard in ranks below the tower.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wei and the princess rushed the emperor to Xuánwu Gate tower, summoned Liu Renjing and others, and posted the remaining Flying Cavalry—over a hundred men—below the tower.

sentences.zh: 俄而多祚等兵至，欲突玄武門樓，宿衛者拒之；

translations.literal: Soon Duozuo's troops arrived and tried to storm Xuánwu Gate tower; the palace guards resisted them;
translations.idiomatic: Soon Duozuo's troops arrived and tried to storm the tower, but the guards held them off;

sentences.zh: 不得進。

translations.literal: they could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: and they could not advance.

sentences.zh: 帝據檻呼多祚等所將千騎，謂曰：“汝並是我爪牙，何故作逆？

translations.literal: The emperor leaned on the railing and called to the Thousand Riders led by Duozuo and others, saying, "You are all my claws and teeth—why commit treason?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor leaned on the railing and called to Duozuo's Thousand Riders, "You are all my own men—why rebel?"

sentences.zh: 若能歸順，斬多祚等，與汝富貴。

translations.literal: If you can return to loyalty and behead Duozuo and the others, I will grant you wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: If you return to loyalty and kill Duozuo and the rest, I will reward you with wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: ”於是千騎王歡喜等倒戈，斬多祚及李承況、獨孤禕之、沙吒忠義等於樓下，餘黨遂潰散。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Thousand Rider Wang Huanxi and others turned their blades; they beheaded Duozuo, Li Chengkang, Dugu Yizhi, Shazha Zhongyi, and others below the tower, and the remaining party then scattered in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand Rider Wang Huanxi and others turned on their leaders, beheaded Duozuo, Li Chengkang, Dugu Yizhi, Shazha Zhongyi, and others below the tower, and the rest fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 重俊既敗，率其屬百餘騎趨肅章門，奔終南山。

translations.literal: When Chongjun had been defeated, he led more than a hundred riders of his followers toward Su Zhang Gate and fled to Zhongnan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, Chongjun led more than a hundred followers toward Su Zhang Gate and fled to Zhongnan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 帝令長上果毅趙思慎率輕騎追之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Senior Commander Zhao Sizhen to lead light cavalry in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Senior Commander Zhao Sizhen to pursue with light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 重俊至雩縣西十餘里，騎不能屬，唯從奴數人。

translations.literal: Chongjun reached more than ten li west of Yuxian; riders could not keep up—only a few attendant slaves remained.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjun reached a spot west of Yuxian, but his riders could not keep pace—only a few servants remained.

sentences.zh: 會日暮憩林下，為左右所殺。

translations.literal: At dusk he rested beneath the trees and was killed by those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he rested in the woods and was killed by his own attendants.

sentences.zh: 製今梟首於朝，又獻之於太廟，並以祭三思、崇訓屍柩。

translations.literal: An edict now exposed his head in the court, also presented it in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and used it together to sacrifice before the coffins of Sansi and Chongxun.
translations.idiomatic: An edict exposed his head at court, presented it at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and used it in sacrifice before the coffins of Sansi and Chongxun.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，下製曰：“朕聞曾氏之孝也，慈親惑於疑聽；

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he issued an edict saying, "We have heard that in the filial piety of the Zeng clan, the loving parent was misled by doubtful hearing;"
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, he issued an edict: "I have heard that in the Zeng family's filial piety, a loving parent may be misled by suspicion;"

sentences.zh: 趙虜之族也，明主哀而望思。

translations.literal: among the clan of the Zhao captive, enlightened rulers mourned and yearned in remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: and among the clan of the captive king of Zhao, enlightened rulers mourned and longed for the lost.

sentences.zh: 曆考前聞，率由舊典。

translations.literal: Examining former reports throughout history, all follow the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing precedents of old, all follow established precedent.

sentences.zh: 重俊，大行之子，元良守器。

translations.literal: Chongjun was the son of the late emperor, the heir who guarded the vessel of state.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjun was the late emperor's son, the heir who held the vessel of state.

sentences.zh: 往罹構間，困於讒嫉。

translations.literal: In the past he suffered framing and alienation and was trapped by slander and jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: He had been framed and trapped by slander and jealousy.

sentences.zh: 莫顧鈇鉞，輕盜甲兵，有此誅夷，無不悲惋。

translations.literal: He did not heed axe and halberd, lightly stole armor and weapons—having this execution, none do not grieve and lament.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored the law, lightly seized arms, and met execution—all mourn him.

sentences.zh: 今四凶咸服，十起何追，方申赤軍之冤，以紓黃泉之痛。

translations.literal: Now the Four Evils are all subdued; the many indictments that arose—why pursue them further? We are about to vindicate the grievance of the red-clad troops and ease the pain of those in the yellow springs.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the villainous faction is destroyed and countless charges need no further pursuit, we shall vindicate his loyal followers and ease the grief of the dead.

sentences.zh: 可贈皇太子。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously to be made crown prince."

sentences.zh: ”諡曰節湣，陪葬定陵。

translations.literal: " His posthumous name was Jiemin, and he was buried beside Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Jiemin, and he was buried beside Dingling.

sentences.zh: 一子宗暉，開元初封湖陽郡王。

translations.literal: He had one son, Zonghui, who early in Kaiyuan was enfeoffed as Prince of Huyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He had one son, Zonghui, enfeoffed as Prince of Huyang early in the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 初，重俊被害，宮府僚吏莫敢近者，永和丞甯嘉勖解衣裹重俊首號哭，時人義之。

translations.literal: At first, when Chongjun was killed, none of the palace establishment staff dared approach; Yonghe Assistant Magistrate Ning Jiaxu removed his garment to wrap Chongjun's head and wailed; people of the time honored his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongjun was killed, none of his palace staff dared approach. Yonghe Assistant Magistrate Ning Jiaxu stripped off his robe to wrap the prince's head and wailed over it. The people praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客聞而大怒，收付製獄，貶為平興丞，尋卒。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke heard and was greatly enraged; he had him taken into the imperial prison, demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Pingxing, and he soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke heard of it and in rage had him imprisoned, then demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Pingxing. He soon died.

sentences.zh: 睿宗踐祚，下製曰：“寧嘉勖能重名節，事高欒、向，幽塗已往，生氣凜然。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he issued an edict saying, "Ning Jiaxu was able to prize integrity and principle; his deed ranks above Luan and Xiang; the dark path has passed, yet living spirit stands stern."
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, he issued an edict: "Ning Jiaxu prized integrity above life; his deed ranks with Luan and Xiang. Though he has passed into the dark, his spirit still stands stern."

sentences.zh: 靜言忠義，追存褒寵。

translations.literal: Quietly speaking of loyalty and righteousness, we posthumously grant praise and favor.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his loyalty and righteousness, we posthumously honor him.

sentences.zh: 可贈永和縣令。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Magistrate of Yonghe County."
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously made Magistrate of Yonghe County."

sentences.zh: ”宗暉，天寶中為衛尉員外卿。

translations.literal: " Zonghui, during Tianbao served as Vice Director of the Imperial Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui served as Vice Director of the Imperial Workshops during the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 十一載，王鉷反，宗暉以賣宅與鉷，貶涪川郡長史，量移盧陽長史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when Wang Hong rebelled, Zonghui was demoted to Administrator of Fuchuan commandery for selling a residence to Hong, then transferred by quota to Administrator of Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 752, when Wang Hong rebelled, Zonghui was demoted to Administrator of Fuchuan for selling him a house, then transferred to Administrator of Luyang.

sentences.zh: 至德元年，追赴行在所，授特進、鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was summoned to the mobile court and appointed Special Advancement and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In 756 he was summoned to the emperor's camp and appointed Special Advancement and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 宗暉無他才，以外族之親，受恩顧轉隆。

translations.literal: Zonghui had no other talent; through kinship as a maternal relative, he received favor and care that grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui had little talent but, as a maternal relative, received ever greater favor.

sentences.zh: 太常員外卿卒。

translations.literal: He died while Vice Director of the Grand Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Vice Director of the Grand Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 殤皇帝 重茂

translations.literal: Short-lived Emperor Chongmao
translations.idiomatic: Short-lived Emperor Chongmao

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：前代以嬖婦孽子破國亡家者多矣，然未如大帝、孝和之甚也。

translations.literal: The historian says: In former ages many were ruined in state and family by favored women and wicked sons, yet none so extreme as the Great Emperor and Xiaohé.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: In earlier ages many dynasties were ruined by favored consorts and wicked sons, but none so severely as under Wu Zetian and Emperor Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 高宗八子，二王早世，為武后所斃者四人，章懷以母子之愛，穎悟之賢，猶不免於虎口。

translations.literal: Of Gaozong's eight sons, two princes died young and four were killed by Empress Wu; Zhanghuai, with mother-son affection and keen, perceptive worth, still did not escape the tiger's maw.
translations.idiomatic: Of Gaozong's eight sons, two died young and four were killed by Wu Zetian. Zhanghuai, for all his mother's love and his bright talent, still did not escape her jaws.

sentences.zh: 況燕、澤、素節異腹之胤乎！

translations.literal: How much more the sons of different wombs—Yan, Ze, and Sujie!
translations.idiomatic: How much less could Yan, Ze, and Sujie—sons of other mothers—hope to survive!

sentences.zh: 覆載胡心，產茲鴆毒，悲夫！

translations.literal: Heaven and earth harbored a barbarous heart and produced this viper's venom—how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth bred a savage heart and produced this poison—lamentable indeed!

sentences.zh: 孝和母囂，婦傲女暴，如置身群魅之中，安有保其終吉哉！

translations.literal: Xiaohé's mother was arrogant, his wife proud and his daughter violent—as if placed among a host of demons; how could he preserve his final good fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong's mother was overbearing, his wife arrogant, his daughter violent—as if he lived among demons. How could he end well!

sentences.zh: 天將滌蕩昏氛，非重茂所能支也。

translations.literal: Heaven was about to cleanse the murky atmosphere—this was not something Chongmao could sustain.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven was about to clear the murky air—Chongmao could not have sustained it.

sentences.zh: 讚曰：父子天性，嬖能害正。

translations.literal: In praise it is said: Father and son share heaven's nature, yet favorites can harm what is right.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Father and son share nature's bond, yet favorites can destroy what is right.

sentences.zh: 宜臼、申生，翻為不令。

translations.literal: Yijiu and Shensheng were turned into unworthy sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yijiu and Shensheng were turned into unworthy sons.

sentences.zh: 唐年鈞德，章懷最仁。

translations.literal: In Tang's years of balanced virtue, Zhanghuai was most humane.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang's age of measured virtue, Zhanghuai was the most humane.

sentences.zh: 凶母畏明，取樂於身。

translations.literal: The vicious mother feared the bright; she took pleasure for herself alone.
translations.idiomatic: The vicious mother feared the bright prince and sought only her own pleasure.
